svg.title: Smoothing: estimate unseen mass, then reward new contexts
svg.desc: Good–Turing estimates unseen probability mass as N1/N and discounts rare counts using frequency-of-frequencies. Kneser–Ney uses continuation probability: the number of distinct left contexts a word completes. In the example, coffee has more distinct contexts than the more frequent word Angeles.

g.text: Smoothing: estimate unseen mass, then reward new contexts
Good–Turing uses frequency-of-frequencies; Kneser–Ney uses distinct left contexts.
the freed mass estimates unseen events.
words a token can follow—not raw frequency.
